Fishing boats knocked against the pier while the tide pulled at their ropes, and the smell of salt and diesel drifted up the narrow streets. At the bakery on the corner, Mara lit the ovens before dawn, as her grandmother had done for forty years, and set out the long wooden trays that still carried the marks of a thousand loaves.
